Adaptive (nearest-neighbour) spatial bandwidth for each event

Source: R/bandwidth.R
adaptive_bandwidth.Rd

For every point, the bandwidth is the distance to its k-th nearest neighbour among neighbours at least min_dist away (this skips near-duplicate/co-located points, e.g. events geocoded to the same address), floored at min_bandwidth.

Usage

adaptive_bandwidth(
  x,
  y,
  k = 5,
  min_dist = 150,
  min_bandwidth = 250,
  k_search = 50
)

Arguments

x, y

Numeric vectors of projected event coordinates (same length).

k

Which nearest neighbour (beyond min_dist) to use; default 5.

min_dist

Minimum distance for a neighbour to be considered (neighbours closer than this are ignored), in the linear units of the working CRS (metres for a UTM projection); default 150, i.e. 150 m.

min_bandwidth

Floor applied to every bandwidth, in the linear units of the working CRS (metres for a UTM projection); default 250, i.e. 250 m.

k_search

How many nearest neighbours to search over before filtering by min_dist; increase this if a warning about insufficient neighbours is raised. Default 50.

Value

A numeric vector of bandwidths, one per input point.

Examples

xy <- sf::st_coordinates(sim_events)
bw <- adaptive_bandwidth(xy[, 1], xy[, 2], k = 5, min_dist = 150,
                         min_bandwidth = 300)
summary(bw)
#>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
#>   300.0   300.0   352.3   469.8   507.7  2057.0
